ami.fallback: without a pin, the newest available image whose name matches, resolved at launch
ami.name_prefix: Deep Learning Base OSS Nvidia Driver GPU AMI (Ubuntu 24.04)
ami.name_regex: ^Deep Learning Base OSS Nvidia Driver GPU AMI \(Ubuntu 24\.04\) [0-9]{8}$
ami.pinned: by the integrator: one describe-images call, then gpu.sh launch --ami <id> or RECEIPTS_GPU_AMI

client: RECEIPTS_GLIMMER_URL=http://<private ip>:8000/v1 on the eval VM (gpu.sh url prints it)
egress: TCP 443 until the server is up, then none (gpu.sh seal)
if_quota_slips: If the G and VT quota (AWS case 179312451500652) is not granted before the pilot, run the Glimmer arm on Modal instead: Modal lists Muse Glimmer 30B BF16 as a dedicated endpoint on an RTX PRO 6000 at $0.000842 per second ($3.03/h; research/open-weights-2026-10-27.md, unverified whether the event credit covers it). Deploy the same image and arguments (gpu-plan.json: serve_args, the two pinned revisions), give the endpoint Modal's own auth token, and point RECEIPTS_GLIMMER_URL at it from the eval VM. What changes: the endpoint is on the internet behind a token instead of inside the eval VM's security group, and the token is a secret the orchestrator holds and no sandbox sees. The arm, its seed, step limit and the move rule stay as pilot.json fixes them.
reachable_from: the eval VM's security group only, on 8000/tcp (vLLM) and 22/tcp (SSH through the eval VM)
recipe_departure: no --reasoning-parser: with it, vLLM 0.28.0 never applies response_format json_schema
stop: gpu.sh stop after the pilot; terminate after the final if the arm moves, or after the pilot if not
